nodes.description: In more than 80% of semantic dementia cases, neurodegeneration is driven by frontotemporal lobar degeneration with TDP-43 type C pathology (FTLD-TDP type C), characterized by cytoplasmic mislocalization of phosphorylated TDP-43, impaired TDP-43 splicing regulation, annexin A11 (ANXA11) and TDP-43 co-dysregulation/co-aggregation, and abundant long dystrophic neurites throughout the cerebral cortex (especially superficial cortical laminae of the anterior temporal lobes). In rare cases, low-level somatic TARDBP variants in cortical regions and the dentate gyrus directly disrupt TDP-43 splicing regulation and subcellular localization.

nodes.description: Asymmetric degeneration of the polar, medial, and inferolateral temporal neocortex and amygdala (with relative sparing of the hippocampal complex in early stages) underlies semantic dementia. In vivo staging of FTLD-TDP type C pathology defines four sequential anatomical stages: Stage 1 involves atrophy in the left amygdala, medial temporal cortex, temporal pole, lateral temporal cortex, and right medial temporal cortex; Stage 2 extends to the left supratemporal cortex; Stage 3 involves the right anterior insula; and Stage 4 reaches the right nucleus accumbens. Left-predominant temporal atrophy primarily drives word comprehension deficits and anomia, whereas right-predominant temporal atrophy drives progressive prosopagnosia and personality/behavioral changes.

evidence.reference_title: In vivo staging of frontotemporal lobar degeneration TDP-43 type C pathology
evidence.snippet: Four sequential stages were identified in the initial development phase. Stage 1 was defined by atrophy in the left amygdala, medial temporal cortex, temporal pole, lateral temporal cortex and right medial temporal cortex; Stage 2 by atrophy in the left supratemporal cortex; Stage 3 by atrophy in the right anterior insula; and Stage 4 by atrophy in the right accumbens.
